They did, the fuel is coming out of a wing dumping point, which means someone hit a switch in the cockpit. Either that or someone on the ground hit the wing and put a hole in it.

From the location of the leak, it looks like the fuel was coming from a fuel dumping point. These points are used in flight to remove excess fuel and lighten the weight of the aircraft before emergency landings. This means a switch was flipped in the cockpit, likely after the ground inspection, and more than likely a mistake.

It's also worth noting from the video that it looks like the plane was still at the gate, not about to take off, and probable that the pilots knew about it because they'd be talking to the ground crew. It's also possible that they didn't know about it because neither pilot was listening to ground at that moment. I'd be interested to know what actually happened here.

Not unusual. Used to pre-fill the wings on a few flights in the morning. This being an overseas flight you'd have instructions at 330 or 430 am too fill the wings to shut off. Later when the load is determined you only have to send one fueler to top off center tank, tail and maybe trim tanks.

But as you see it's much later; sun is coming up and hits those wings and warms them up. Fuel expands and gets dumped out the overflow. Poor planning, heck of a mess: rarely dangerous.
